summary: Verified both bug fixes end-to-end. (1) Box large-file download — 3 mocked tests in TestBoxLargeFile PASS: proxy-first now bypasses the predefined BOX_DOWNLOAD_FILE action entirely (its inline-base64 envelope cap can no longer trigger), HTTPException 502 from the predefined action falls through to proxy and records an actionable per-file error without crashing the whole sync, and the 60 MB sample mirrors under the new 500 MB sanity cap (raised from 50 MB). (2) Findings background job — 4 mocked tests in TestFindingsBackgroundJob PASS: the new _run_findings_job task transitions pending→running→completed and writes deal_room_findings rows, Claude exceptions mark the job 'failed' (never silently stuck on running), an in-flight job is returned instead of spawning a duplicate, and the HTTP handler returns in <0.5s with no synchronous Claude await. All 19 prior backend regression tests (test_box_recursive_sync, test_folder_picker, test_preview_images) still pass. LIVE smoke against the preview backend with Alex (buyer): 4 live tests in test_findings_job_live.py PASS — POST /generate-findings returns in well under 1s with {job_id, status:'pending', files_to_analyze:8, already_running:false}; the in-flight branch is returned correctly on the second click; polling reaches 'completed' (Claude pass ~10s for 8 files); GET /findings-job (latest) returns the most recent job. The new `findings_jobs` Mongo collection is alive (6 completed rows observed after the live run, all with duration_ms in 9817-13326 ms range and findings_count=5/files_analyzed=8 — no Cloudflare 524 anywhere). FRONTEND smoke as Alex: login → /app/dashboard → /app/rooms (8 rooms render) → clicked Backfill Test Co → DealRoomDetail rendered cleanly with ZERO JS console errors, ZERO page errors. Code review of /app/frontend/src/pages/DealRoomDetail.jsx confirms the mount-time job-resume useEffect (lines 54-85) re-attaches to any pending/running job and toasts 'Resuming analysis already in progress…', and generateFindings (lines 190-235) polls every 2500ms with no client-side timeout and degrades on transient network blips (catch/continue). Total: 30/30 tests passing (7 new + 19 regression + 4 live). Backend success rate 100%, Frontend smoke 100%.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 10,226 lines — _run_findings_job (7307-7430) and the generate-findings POST + GET endpoints (7434-7510) should be extracted into backend/jobs/findings.py alongside a generic AsyncJobQueue helper. The same background-task pattern (POST kicks task, persisted status doc, poll endpoint) will be needed for any other long Claude call (research briefs, outreach generation) and re-inventing it inline each time is a maintenance trap.

_run_findings_job has no cleanup task for old findings_jobs rows. The review_request acknowledges this is 'acceptable — rows are small' but a TTL index on `created_at` (e.g. 30 days) would prevent unbounded growth without writing a sweeper. One-line fix: db.findings_jobs.create_index('created_at', expireAfterSeconds=30*86400) in the startup event.

If two findings-job POSTs arrive within ~50 ms of each other for the same room (e.g. double-click), the inflight check at server.py:7456 races: both requests can find {} from the find_one and both can insert+spawn. A unique partial index `{room_id:1, status:1}` filtered to status in pending/running would make the duplicate insert fail and convert the second handler into the already_running branch deterministically. Low-frequency, but the only remaining hole in the dedup story.

Frontend lib/uploadConfig.js still hard-codes UPLOAD_MAX_MB=50 for the direct deal-room file upload form. This is a DIFFERENT code path from the external-source sync (where the cap was raised to 500 MB), so it's not a contradiction — but if the user's complaint 'no limit to the payload amount' also covered direct uploads, this needs a separate fix in /api/deal-rooms/{rid}/files. Verify which path triggered the original 50 MB friction before bumping it.

_run_findings_job at server.py:7322 caps `files` to `.to_list(50)` — institutional vaults can hold hundreds of files; the docstring at 7313 says 'no per-job time cap … the Claude pass may legitimately take several minutes' but the file slice silently truncates inventory at 50. Either remove the cap or surface it in the response/job doc so the buyer knows their 200-file vault was analyzed against only the oldest 50.

context_for_next_testing_agent: test_findings_job_live.py is the canonical live regression for the findings background job. Run via `cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/test_findings_job_live.py -v -p no:warnings`. The test uses Alex's pre-existing deal rooms — does NOT seed any new rooms — and tolerates the transient Cloudflare/ingress ReadTimeout that occasionally hits the preview backend (it retries POST once with a 30s timeout, and the polling loop catches ReadTimeout and continues). DO NOT combine this file with the mocked test_large_files_and_findings_job.py file in a single pytest invocation if you start hitting motor 'Future attached to a different loop' issues — run them as separate invocations. The findings_jobs collection now persists indefinitely; consider adding a TTL index per critical_code_review_comments[1].
rca of the issue: N/A — this iteration validates two bug fixes (Box payload-too-large + findings 524). Both fixes verified end-to-end. Original RCAs (documented in the test file header): (1) Composio's predefined BOX_DOWNLOAD_FILE inlines the file as base64 in its JSON envelope, hitting a ~10 MB ceiling; the fix bypasses it by trying Composio's Proxy Execute path FIRST (which streams via R2 with no cap) and only falls back to the predefined action when proxy is unavailable. The 50 MB sanity cap was also raised to 500 MB per user request. (2) POST /generate-findings was awaiting the Claude call synchronously, exceeding Cloudflare's 100s edge timeout for any vault with >5-10 files; the fix wraps the work in an asyncio.create_task background job, returns a job_id immediately, and exposes GET /findings-job/{job_id} + GET /findings-job (latest) for polling. The frontend polls every 2500ms with no client-side timeout and reconnects to the same job on page reload.
